interactions.summary: Students try to explain Peter's rage as a response to church chaos or Dante's own feelings, while Jiang keeps returning to the deeper problem: heaven's first pope should embody divine mercy, yet the passage still erupts into a curse against the pope on earth.

A student suggests the outburst is a dramatic device and another begins to warn against false gods, but Jiang insists the dissonance is memorable precisely because Peter cannot forgive the pope even though church corruption and indulgences were already obvious to everyone.

claims.claim: Jiang says the real paradox is not Peter's anger by itself but the fact that someone in heaven, standing in the presence of an all-loving and forgiving God, is cursing God's earthly representative.
He concedes that Dante's exile and hatred of the Pope may be bleeding into the scene as vengeance, yet he still asks the class to extend grace and assume the poet is trying to speak for God.
Jiang says the purpose of this heavenly anti-papal outburst remains unresolved and has baffled scholars for a long time.

Jiang partly accepts that the passage is unforgettable because of its dissonance, but he rejects the idea that it merely warns about corruption because indulgences and church abuse were already publicly blatant.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang voices the shock without smoothing it over: the scene is so strange he jokes that scholars are left wondering whether Dante was drunk when he wrote it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Was Dante drunk when he wrote this?
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This preserves how aggressively unresolved Jiang keeps the heavenly anti-papal paradox.

signature_moments.moment: The contradiction is sharpened to a single refusal: Peter cannot forgive the pope.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Yet Peter cannot forgive the Pope
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest statement of the moral contradiction driving the whole discussion.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for the unforgettable clash between heaven's mercy and Peter's continued anti-papal fury.

uncertainty_notes.note: Two student comments are ASR-fragmented, but Jiang's replies make the surrounding interpretive options clear.
